note: Per-route performance ceilings. Read docs/PERFORMANCE_BUDGETS.md before changing a number: down is free, up is a decision.

method.countedUpTo: route interactive: its readiness gate, no earlier than the window load event. A resource counts if it STARTED before that moment, so the post-paint background warmup is excluded by construction rather than by how fast the box is.

routes.why: The landing every shared link and every search result opens.

The product. Its data loads client side, so the document is a shell and must stay one. This lane measured 3066 KB eager JS decoded, down 634 KB from 3700 KB. The remaining 166 KB would defer slim index, MapLibre, or pin-price paths, so the runtime ceiling stays 3400 KB and e2e/map-perf-budget.spec.ts owns the proof.

pinReady.note: Cold first visit on phone; pinReadyMs from e2e/mobile-map-chrome-fit.spec.ts on a SwiftShader production build. 634 KB eager-JS reduction (3700→3066 KB decoded) does not touch basemap style/tile/glyph init, which remains the pin-ready bottleneck (~9.8s on this harness). A prior interrupted run recorded 32200 ms and was discarded.

routes.why: The morning brief, composed on the server from bundled data. Its server figure is the loosest here because it is the one route that really composes something.
The fastest route we have. It is the shape every other route is held against.
The Out tab shell. Composed from existing what's-on rows; no new API.

The page that states what the figures mean and where they come from, linked from every trust claim on the site. It composes nothing per request, so it is the floor a server-rendered page here should sit on.

The one launch surface whose server render was not a shell: it re-parsed the 6.7 MB price dataset per request until the shared priced-venue index was reused. The ceiling is here so that read cannot come back unnoticed.
